# Open questions for the client

Every point where the brief at `.brain/requirements/BRIEF.md` does not actually
settle what it appears to settle, phrased as a question you can answer in a
sentence.

**Nothing here has been decided.** Each question below is open, and each one
blocks the requirement it affects from moving past `draft`. The same list
appears in the `ambiguities` field of every requirement in `book.yaml`; the two
must not diverge.

Sentence numbers refer to the six sentences of the brief as recorded in
`BRIEF.md`.

---

## Book ID: typed in by the user, or generated by the application?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-002, REQ-BOOK-006, REQ-BOOK-008, REQ-BOOK-017
- **The document says:** "with each book card showing the Book ID, Name, Author,
  Language, and Price" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2) — and, of the form, only "where
  users can enter the book details" (BRIEF.md, sentence 3).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The Book ID is one of the details the user types into the Add Book form,
    like Name and Author.
  - (b) The Book ID is produced by the application when the Book is added, and
    the user never sees it until the book card appears.
- **Question for the client:** Is the Book ID typed in by the person adding the
  Book, or produced by the application itself?
- **Why it matters:** (a) needs a form field, a uniqueness check on submission,
  and an error message the user can act on when the ID is taken. (b) needs none
  of those but does need a generation scheme, and the two produce different
  looking IDs on every existing Book — so switching later means either
  rewriting stored data or living with two ID styles side by side in the
  gallery.

## What should a Book ID look like?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-017
- **The document says:** "with each book card showing the Book ID" (BRIEF.md,
  sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) A plain counter — 1, 2, 3 — meaningful only inside this application.
  - (b) A real-world book identifier such as an ISBN, which the user knows and
    may want to search by.
  - (c) An opaque code (for example a UUID) that is guaranteed unique but is not
    meant to be read or typed.
- **Question for the client:** What should a Book ID look like — a number, a
  code you supply, an ISBN, or something else?
- **Why it matters:** (b) carries a fixed format that must be validated and can
  legitimately be duplicated across editions; (c) is long and unreadable on a
  card, which changes the card layout; (a) is neither. The choice also decides
  whether the ID can ever be searched or typed by a user.

## May a deleted Book's Book ID be reused?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-010, REQ-BOOK-017
- **The document says:** "Each book should have a Delete button to remove it
  from the library." (BRIEF.md, sentence 5)
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The ID is released when the Book is deleted, and the next Book added may
    receive it.
  - (b) The ID is spent permanently; no later Book ever carries it again.
- **Question for the client:** May a deleted Book's Book ID be given to a later
  Book, or is it used up forever?
- **Why it matters:** Under (a), anyone who wrote down a Book ID — in a
  bookmark, an export, a note — may later find it pointing at a different book,
  with no way to tell. (b) rules that out but requires the store to remember
  which IDs have been used, which is a different data shape from a simple list.

## Is "Name" the book's title?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-002, REQ-BOOK-006
- **The document says:** "with each book card showing the Book ID, Name, Author,
  Language, and Price" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) "Name" is the book's title, and the word "Title" would mean the same
    thing.
  - (b) "Name" is something else — a display name, a series name, or a short
    label distinct from the full title.
- **Question for the client:** Is "Name" the title of the book, or something
  other than the title?
- **Why it matters:** If it is the title, the field is long, may need to wrap
  over two lines on a card, and would be the natural thing to sort or search by.
  If it is a short label, a separate Title field is missing from the brief
  entirely — which is a new field, a new form input and a new card row, found
  after the layout is built.

## Language: free text, or a fixed list?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-002, REQ-BOOK-006, REQ-BOOK-007
- **The document says:** "with each book card showing the Book ID, Name, Author,
  Language, and Price" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The user types whatever they like, so "Bangla", "bangla" and "Bengali"
    can all end up in the Library.
  - (b) The user picks from a list you supply, so the values are consistent.
- **Question for the client:** Is Language typed in freely, or chosen from a
  fixed list of languages you will supply?
- **Why it matters:** (b) needs the list itself, which only you can supply, plus
  a decision about what happens to a language that is not on it. (a) costs
  nothing now, but the values can never be grouped, filtered or counted by
  language without someone cleaning up every record by hand — and that cleanup
  grows with the Library.

## Price: what currency, how many decimals, what range?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-002, REQ-BOOK-006, REQ-BOOK-007
- **The document says:** "with each book card showing the Book ID, Name, Author,
  Language, and Price" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) A single fixed currency for the whole Library, shown with a symbol the
    application supplies.
  - (b) A currency chosen per Book, which means a currency field the brief never
    mentions.
  - (c) A plain number with no currency at all.
- **Question for the client:** What currency is Price in, should it show decimal
  places, and is there a lowest or highest allowed value?
- **Why it matters:** (b) adds a field to the form, the card and the store.
  Decimals decide whether the value is stored as a whole number of the smallest
  unit or as a decimal — getting that wrong shows up as rounding errors that
  cannot be corrected after the fact. And with no range, "-5" and
  "99999999999" are both accepted today.

## Which fields must be filled in?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-006, REQ-BOOK-007
- **The document says:** "a popup/modal form where users can enter the book
  details" (BRIEF.md, sentence 3).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Every field is required, and the form refuses a submission with any
    field left blank.
  - (b) Only some are required — perhaps Name and Author — and the rest may be
    filled in later or left empty.
- **Question for the client:** Which of Name, Author, Language and Price must be
  filled in before a Book can be added, and which may be left blank?
- **Why it matters:** Under (b), every book card must have a sensible way of
  showing a missing Price or Language, and the brief gives none. Tightening from
  (b) to (a) afterwards is also blocked by any Books already stored with blank
  fields.

## May two identical Books exist?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-008
- **The document says:** "After submitting the form, the new book should be
  added to the library and immediately displayed in the gallery." (BRIEF.md,
  sentence 4)
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Every submission adds a Book, even if the Library already holds one with
    the same Name and Author — a library may hold several copies.
  - (b) A submission matching an existing Book is refused, or updates the
    existing one.
- **Question for the client:** May two Books with the same Name and Author both
  exist in the Library, or should the second one be refused?
- **Why it matters:** (b) needs a rule for what counts as "the same book" — Name
  alone, Name and Author, or the Book ID — plus an error path in the form.
  Adding that rule later cannot clean up the duplicates already stored.

## Where does the "simple data store" live — the server, or the browser?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-008, REQ-BOOK-012
- **The document says:** "The application should be simple, responsive, easy to
  run on a local development PC, use a simple data store" (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The Books are held by the Node.js application — in a file or an embedded
    database — so anyone opening the page sees the same Library.
  - (b) The Books are held in the user's own browser storage, so each browser has
    its own Library and the Node.js part only serves the page.
- **Question for the client:** Does the data store live on the Node.js server,
  or in the user's own browser?
- **Why it matters:** This decides whether the application needs an API at all.
  (b) has no endpoints, no server-side validation and no shared data; (a) has all
  three. Moving from (b) to (a) later is a rewrite of the add and delete paths,
  and the Books already saved in someone's browser do not come with it.

## Must the Books survive a restart?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-012
- **The document says:** "use a simple data store" (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) "Simple" means in-memory: stopping the application loses every Book, and
    that is acceptable for a local development tool.
  - (b) "Simple" means a file or small embedded database: the Books are still
    there after a restart.
- **Question for the client:** Must Books still be there after the application is
  stopped and started again, or is losing them on restart acceptable?
- **Why it matters:** (a) is a few lines and no file handling; (b) needs a file
  format, a read on startup, a write on every change, and a decision about what
  happens when that file is missing or corrupt. It also decides whether a
  developer restarting the app loses their test data every time — which is a
  demo risk, not just a technical one.

## Delete: permanent, or recoverable?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-010
- **The document says:** "Each book should have a Delete button to remove it
  from the library." (BRIEF.md, sentence 5)
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The Book is erased from the data store and is unrecoverable.
  - (b) The Book is marked as removed and hidden from the gallery, but is still
    held and could be restored.
- **Question for the client:** Is a deleted Book gone permanently, or should it
  be recoverable, and by whom?
- **Why it matters:** (b) needs a status field on every Book, a filter on every
  read, and somewhere to restore from — none of which can be added to data that
  (a) has already erased. Given there is no confirmation step settled either
  (see below), a mis-click under (a) is unrecoverable.

## Should Delete ask for confirmation?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-010, REQ-BOOK-011
- **The document says:** "Each book should have a Delete button to remove it
  from the library." (BRIEF.md, sentence 5)
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) One click removes the Book straight away.
  - (b) A confirmation is shown first, and the Book is removed only if the user
    confirms.
- **Question for the client:** Should the user be asked to confirm before a Book
  is deleted, or should the Delete button remove it straight away?
- **Why it matters:** With Delete sitting on every card in a dense grid, (a)
  makes an accidental deletion one mis-click away and — if deletion is permanent
  — unrecoverable. (b) is a second dialog to build, style and make responsive,
  and it changes what "user-friendly" means for the whole gallery.

## What does the home page show when the Library is empty?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-001, REQ-BOOK-004, REQ-BOOK-011
- **The document says:** "The home page should display all books in a clean and
  attractive gallery/grid layout" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) A blank area below the "+ Add Book" button.
  - (b) A message inviting the user to add their first Book.
- **Question for the client:** What should the home page show when the Library
  holds no Books at all?
- **Why it matters:** This is the first screen anyone sees on a fresh install and
  the screen after the last Book is deleted. Under (a) a new user cannot tell an
  empty Library from a broken page, which is exactly the impression a demo should
  not give.

## In what order should the Books appear?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-001
- **The document says:** "The home page should display all books in a clean and
  attractive gallery/grid layout" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Newest first, so a Book just added appears at the top of the gallery.
  - (b) Oldest first, so it appears at the bottom.
  - (c) Sorted by Name, Author or Price.
- **Question for the client:** In what order should the book cards appear in the
  gallery?
- **Why it matters:** The brief requires a new Book to be "immediately
  displayed" — under (b) or (c) it may land off-screen, and the user cannot tell
  whether the add worked. (c) also needs a rule for sorting non-Latin text and
  for Books with a blank value in the sort field.

## Is there a limit on how many Books the gallery shows?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-001
- **The document says:** "The home page should display all books" (BRIEF.md,
  sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Literally all of them, however many there are, on one page.
  - (b) A page at a time, with paging or infinite scroll once the Library grows.
- **Question for the client:** Is there an upper limit on how many Books the
  gallery shows at once, or should every Book always be on the page?
- **Why it matters:** (b) is a second set of controls, a different data-loading
  shape, and it interacts with sort order and with a newly added Book appearing
  "immediately" — a new Book on page 4 is not immediately displayed. (a) is
  simpler but becomes unusable at some size nobody has named.

## What do "modern", "clean and attractive" and "user-friendly" require?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-001, REQ-BOOK-002, REQ-BOOK-013
- **The document says:** "Create a simple and modern Book Library application"
  (BRIEF.md, sentence 1); "in a clean and attractive gallery/grid layout"
  (BRIEF.md, sentence 2); "provide a clean and user-friendly interface"
  (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Ordinary tidy defaults are enough: consistent spacing, readable type, a
    card with a border.
  - (b) A specific look is expected — a brand, a colour palette, a font, cover
    images on the cards, hover and transition effects.
- **Question for the client:** What specifically makes the interface "modern",
  "clean and attractive" and "user-friendly" — is there a reference site, brand,
  or design you want it to look like?
- **Why it matters:** No test can check this as written, so it is the one thing
  most likely to be rejected at review after everything else passes. If (b) turns
  out to include cover images, that is a new field on every Book, an upload or
  URL path, and a different card layout — not a styling pass.

## Which screen sizes must "responsive" cover?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-013
- **The document says:** "The application should be simple, responsive, easy to
  run on a local development PC" (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The desktop layout simply reflows when the browser window is resized —
    responsive on a development PC, which is the only machine the brief names.
  - (b) It is genuinely usable on a phone and a tablet, tested on real devices.
- **Question for the client:** Which screen widths or devices must the
  application work on, and what is the narrowest one that must be supported?
- **Why it matters:** (b) sets a testable minimum width and brings touch target
  sizes, a modal that fits a small screen, and device testing into scope. Without
  a number, "responsive" cannot be signed off or disputed — which means it will
  be disputed at handover.

## Who may add and delete Books, and is the Library shared?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-001, REQ-BOOK-008, REQ-BOOK-010, REQ-BOOK-012
- **The document says:** "a popup/modal form where users can enter the book
  details" (BRIEF.md, sentence 3).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) There is no sign-in at all: anyone who opens the page sees one shared
    Library and can add or delete anything in it.
  - (b) There are accounts, and "users" means people who are distinguishable from
    one another — each with their own Library, or with different rights over a
    shared one.
- **Question for the client:** Is the Library shared by everyone who opens the
  application, or does each person have their own?
- **Why it matters:** (b) is a whole additional area of work — sign-in,
  sessions, an owner on every Book — and it is the difference between a Delete
  button anyone can press and one that must check who is pressing it. The brief
  mentions no login, but it also never says the Library is public. Retrofitting
  ownership onto Books stored without an owner requires a data migration and a
  decision about who owns the existing ones.

## What does the user see when adding or deleting fails?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-007, REQ-BOOK-008, REQ-BOOK-010
- **The document says:** "After submitting the form, the new book should be
  added to the library and immediately displayed in the gallery." (BRIEF.md,
  sentence 4)
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Failure is out of scope: the brief describes only the success path.
  - (b) A visible error message is expected whenever the store cannot be written
    or the request does not reach the application.
- **Question for the client:** What should the user see when adding or deleting a
  Book fails unexpectedly?
- **Why it matters:** Under (a) a failed add looks identical to a successful one
  until the page is reloaded, and the user re-submits — producing duplicates in
  exactly the case where duplicates are least expected. (b) needs an error area
  in the modal, an error area on the gallery, and wording for both.

## What happens when two people act at the same time?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-008, REQ-BOOK-010, REQ-BOOK-012
- **The document says:** "use a simple data store" (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) One user at a time on a local PC, so simultaneous changes cannot happen
    and nothing needs to guard against them.
  - (b) Several browsers or tabs may be open at once, so two writes can overlap.
- **Question for the client:** If two people add or delete Books at the same
  moment, what should happen?
- **Why it matters:** With a file-based store under (b), two overlapping writes
  can silently lose one of the Books or truncate the file — a class of bug that
  never appears in single-user testing and is very hard to reproduce afterwards.
  (a) means we can skip locking entirely, but only if you confirm it.

## Should the details be validated by the application, or only in the browser?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-007, REQ-BOOK-008
- **The document says:** "a popup/modal form where users can enter the book
  details" (BRIEF.md, sentence 3).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Checking in the browser is enough, since the browser is the only way in.
  - (b) The application checks again before storing, on the basis that anything
    reachable over HTTP can be called without the form.
- **Question for the client:** Should the details be checked only in the browser,
  or checked again by the application before the Book is stored?
- **Why it matters:** Under (a), anyone who can reach the application can store a
  Book with any content at all, including content that breaks the gallery for
  everyone else. Adding server-side checks later does not clean up what was
  already stored. Note this question only arises if the store is server-side —
  see "Where does the simple data store live".

## Must Name and Author accept non-Latin scripts?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-002, REQ-BOOK-006, REQ-BOOK-008
- **The document says:** "with each book card showing the Book ID, Name, Author,
  Language, and Price" (BRIEF.md, sentence 2).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) English text only — the presence of a Language field is incidental.
  - (b) Any script, since a Library with a Language field plainly expects books
    that are not in English.
- **Question for the client:** Must Name and Author accept non-Latin scripts such
  as Bangla or Arabic, or will they only ever be English text?
- **Why it matters:** (b) constrains the encoding used at every layer — the file
  the store writes, the response headers, the fonts on the card — and a length
  limit counted in bytes rather than characters will silently truncate a Bangla
  title mid-character. Discovering this after data exists means re-encoding
  stored records.

## Can a Book be edited after it has been added?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-008, REQ-BOOK-012
- **The document says:** "After submitting the form, the new book should be
  added to the library" (BRIEF.md, sentence 4); "Each book should have a Delete
  button" (BRIEF.md, sentence 5).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) There is no edit: the brief names Add and Delete only, and a mistake is
    fixed by deleting the Book and adding it again.
  - (b) Edit was assumed and simply not written down, as it usually is alongside
    add and delete.
- **Question for the client:** Should a Book's details be editable after it has
  been added, or is the only correction to delete it and add it again?
- **Why it matters:** (b) is a chargeable addition — a second modal mode, an
  update path in the store, and an Edit control on every card, which changes the
  card layout the gallery is built around. It is better priced now than
  discovered at review. Under (a), correcting a typo destroys the Book ID, which
  interacts with the ID-reuse question above.

## Should the modal close by itself after a Book is added?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-005, REQ-BOOK-009
- **The document says:** "After submitting the form, the new book should be
  added to the library and immediately displayed in the gallery." (BRIEF.md,
  sentence 4)
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The modal closes on success, revealing the gallery with the new card in
    it.
  - (b) The modal stays open and cleared, so several Books can be added in a row.
- **Question for the client:** Should the modal form close by itself once a Book
  has been added successfully?
- **Why it matters:** Under (b) the new card is behind the modal, so "immediately
  displayed" cannot be demonstrated, and a confirmation message inside the modal
  becomes necessary instead. This decides what a user actually experiences after
  every single add.

## How does a user close the modal without adding a Book?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-005
- **The document says:** "Add an "+ Add Book" button on the home page that opens
  a popup/modal form" (BRIEF.md, sentence 3).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) A visible Cancel or close control, and clicking outside or pressing
    Escape also closes it.
  - (b) The only way out is to submit the form.
- **Question for the client:** Should the modal form have a way to cancel and
  close without adding a Book, and if so, what should it be?
- **Why it matters:** Under (b) a user who opens the modal by mistake is trapped
  and will reload the page. If closing by clicking outside is expected, it also
  raises whether the entered details are kept or discarded when the modal is
  reopened — a behaviour that has to be built deliberately either way.

## Does the application need to be accessible?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-003, REQ-BOOK-005, REQ-BOOK-013
- **The document says:** "provide a clean and user-friendly interface"
  (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) "User-friendly" means visually pleasant for a sighted mouse user.
  - (b) It includes keyboard-only operation and screen reader support to a
    recognised standard such as WCAG 2.1 AA.
- **Question for the client:** Does the application need to be usable with a
  keyboard alone and with a screen reader, or is mouse-and-sighted use enough?
- **Why it matters:** A modal is the single hardest component to make accessible
  — focus trapping, focus return, an accessible name, Escape handling — and it
  is far cheaper to build that way than to retrofit. If this application is ever
  used by a public body, (b) may be a legal requirement rather than a
  preference.

## "Avoid unnecessary dependencies" — none at all, or an approved few?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-015
- **The document says:** "avoid unnecessary dependencies" (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Zero third-party runtime packages: only the Node.js standard library.
  - (b) A small number is fine as long as each one earns its place, with a
    framework such as Express being the usual example.
- **Question for the client:** Does "avoid unnecessary dependencies" mean no
  third-party runtime packages at all, or a small set you would approve one by
  one?
- **Why it matters:** (a) means a hand-written HTTP and static-file layer, which
  is more code to write and to review — and hand-rolled static file serving is a
  well-known source of security defects. (b) is faster to build but hands the
  client packages to patch and audit after handover. The two produce
  fundamentally different codebases, so this cannot be deferred.

## Do development and test tools count as dependencies?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-015
- **The document says:** "avoid unnecessary dependencies" (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) The rule applies only to what runs in production; test runners, linters
    and formatters are exempt.
  - (b) The rule applies to everything in the repository.
- **Question for the client:** Do development and testing tools count as
  dependencies for this purpose, or only what ships at runtime?
- **Why it matters:** Under (b) the test framework must be Node's own built-in
  runner and there can be no browser-automation tool, which limits how the
  responsive and modal behaviour can be tested at all. That constrains the test
  strategy before any test is written.

## Node.js: which version, which framework, which port, and is there a build step?

- **Affects:** REQ-BOOK-014, REQ-BOOK-016
- **The document says:** "Create a simple and modern Book Library application
  using Node.js" (BRIEF.md, sentence 1); "easy to run on a local development PC"
  (BRIEF.md, sentence 6).
- **Which could mean:**
  - (a) Plain Node.js, served as written, started with one command and no build
    step.
  - (b) A framework and a front-end toolchain that compiles the source before it
    runs.
- **Question for the client:** Which Node.js version, which web framework (if
  any), which port, and should there be a build step before the application runs?
- **Why it matters:** "Easy to run" is only testable once there is a named
  command, a named port and a stated minimum Node.js version — otherwise it
  fails on the reviewer's machine and nobody can say whose fault that is. A build
  step also decides which of the project's coding-standard rule sets applies,
  which affects every source file.
